title: Remembering a big win can raise your goosebumps

beats.label: goosebumps
lines: Just remembering a big win can raise goosebumps all over your body.
Cold can do it, and so can fear, music, or a horror film.
Tiny muscles at the base of your hairs contract and pull them straight up, a reflex started by your fight-or-flight nerves.

beats.title: Feeling vs. skin
lines: Here's the twist: feeling chills and getting bumps are not the same thing.
In research, the bumps people reported didn't always match the bumps measured.

beats.title: Raised hair in animals
lines: In furry animals, raised hair traps warm air.
Frightened cats and chimpanzees bristle to look bigger.
Porcupines raise their quills when threatened.
And some people can raise goosebumps on purpose, no trigger needed.
Many don't realize not everyone can.
Some call it a leftover reflex, but it may be your body's sign that you were moved.

sources.claim: Feeling or remembering strong positive emotions, such as after winning a sports event, can cause piloerection; emotionally triggered goose bumps tend to occur across the whole body.
Goose bumps can come from cold, fear, music, or watching a horror film.
Arrector pili muscles at the base of hairs contract and pull the hair straight up; the reflex is started by the sympathetic nervous system, responsible for many fight-or-flight responses.
The self-reported feeling of goosebumps does not always correlate with physiological piloerection.
In furred animals erect hairs trap air for insulation and make the animal appear larger to intimidate enemies, seen in chimpanzees and frightened cats; porcupines raise their quills when threatened.
Some people can voluntarily generate piloerection without an external trigger, and those with the ability are frequently unaware that not everyone can.
Goose bumps under stress are considered by some a vestigial reflex; goose bumps are accompanied by a response pattern thought to indicate the emotional state of being moved.

youtube.title: Your goosebumps might know something you don't 🧠
youtube.description: A memory, a song or the cold can make your hair stand up. Here's the tiny reflex behind goosebumps, and why the feeling and the bumps don't always match.
